sources.source_chapter_or_section: Chapter III ("His elephant head and his vehicle, the rat, are usually taken to be emblems of his prudence, sagacity and forethought")

verification.notes: Underhill's Chapter III names the rat as Ganesa's vehicle alongside his elephant head.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Chapter III ("He had no place in Vedic literature, nor in the Ramayana or the older Puranas, and he only later became identified with the Ganas, or attendants on Siva")

verification.notes: Underhill records that Ganesa came to be identified with the Ganas, the attendants on Siva to whom Nandi belongs.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Chapter III ("the correct ceremony includes the gift of a golden elephant, on which are seated golden figures of Siva, Gauri his wife, and Ganesa their son")

verification.notes: Underhill's Gajagauri vrata seats Siva, Gauri his wife, and Ganesa their son together in the golden image group.

note.en: Mahalasa (Mhalsa) is the consort of Khandoba at Jejuri.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: "Champa Shashthi" ("The image of Martand or Martand Bhairav there, is also called Mairal. Its local name is Khanderao, he is the family god of many Marathas. His consort Mhalsahai is riding and seated behind him, and is attended by a dog")

verification.notes: Gupte's Champa Shashthi entry names Mhalsahai as the consort of Khanderao, seated behind him and attended by a dog.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: "Champa Shashthi" ("His consort Mhalsahai is riding and seated behind him... Khanderao is supposed to be riding a yellow horse, his flag is yellow")

verification.notes: Gupte places Mhalsahai beside Martand Bhairav, the form Gupte identifies as an incarnation of Shiva.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: "Champa Shashthi" ("The image of Martand or Martand Bhairav there, is also called Mairal. Its local name is Khanderao, he is the family god of many Marathas. His consort Mhalsahai is riding and seated behind him, and is attended by a dog")

note.en: Lakshmi Narayana is the conjoint form of Lakshmi and Vishnu invoked in the Padma Purana's mantra.

verification.notes: Wilson's preface on the Padma Purana records the potency of the mantra addressed to Lakshmi Narayana, the paired form of the goddess with Vishnu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Preface, "4. The Padma Purana" ("the merits of bathing in the month of Magha, and the potency of the Mantra or prayer addressed to Lakshmi Narayana")

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Anusasana Parva, Section XVII ("Thou art both white and tawny (being as thou art half male and half female)")

verification.notes: The Shiva hymn in Anusasana Parva Section XVII salutes the god as 'both white and tawny (being as thou art half male and half female)'.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("In the present or Vaivaswata Manwantara... he begot, as his sons, the seven Rishis... and was himself the grand-sire of the Gandharbas, serpents, Danavas, and gods")

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XXI ("Muni, of the Apsarasas: and Arishta, of the illustrious Gandharbas. These were the children of Kasyapa, whether movable or stationary")

verification.notes: The Gandharbas are named among the children of Kasyapa in Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter XXI.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCXXV ("Let the great Mothers of the Universe repair to-day to Skanda. They can master at will any degree of energy. Let them kill this child")

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCXXVI ("The planets with their satellites, the Rishis and the Mothers, Agni and numerous other blazing courtiers... waited on Mahasena along with the Mothers")
